title: Taiwan's FSC tells 230 financial firms to complete a cybersecurity self-assessment; police tie 100-plus banking thefts to Android malware, Tech Times reports
date_note: Tech Times dates the FSC briefing and the police press conference to Nov. 26; the page is published Nov. 27.
geo_basis: country as the source states it; Taipei used for the pin
summary: Tech Times reports Taiwan's Financial Supervisory Commission told 230 banks, securities firms, insurers and e-payment operators to finish a 14-item cybersecurity self-assessment by the end of 2026. It also reports more than 100 online-banking theft cases since September, with losses above NT$17.42 million, that involve fake short-drama apps letting attackers remote-control Android phones.
plain: Tech Times reports Taiwan's financial regulator told 230 firms to finish a 14-item security self-check by the end of 2026, while more than 100 banking theft cases involve fake Android apps.
exec: Tech Times reports a regulator-mandated security self-check for 230 financial firms and more than 100 banking theft cases involving fake Android apps.
action: As reported by Tech Times, police advise avoiding apps from unofficial sources and refusing unknown VPN and accessibility permission requests.
